intelligence.human_view: Run 30 filed a note and the very next sync reported zero new notes. The easy reading is "it didn't land" — and the easy reaction is to re-file it, re-run the sync, or dispatch a fix. None of that happened, because the loop checks the bytes before it reacts: the feed says 589 cards, and the 589th is the note itself. A zero in a sync report is a fact about that tick, not a verdict on the note. The discipline is symmetric — doubt the claim when it says four landed, and doubt the zero when it says none did. Both are claims; only the feed is proof. The one honest gap: the log doesn't show which run carried the note between 07:06Z and 07:23Z, and this note says so instead of inventing a mechanism. A record that admits what it doesn't know stays trustworthy.
